text:
Anya (Sales): RetailBank POC failing when they call our private endpoint from behind their corporate outbound proxy. They see 502s and cert errors. Can eng help triage?

Jamal (Eng): Are they using a forward proxy that terminates TLS (TLS inspection) or a CONNECT tunnel?

Anya (Sales): Infra lead says "inline proxy" and egress goes through an appliance that does TLS interception for outbound domains.

Ravi (NetOps): That will break SNI and certs unless the proxy uses CONNECT. Can you paste a curl and openssl s_client capture from their test host?

Anya (Sales): From their dev VM (IPs masked):
```
$ curl -v https://rb-poc.internal.redwood/v1/status
* Rebuilt URL to: https://rb-poc.internal.redwood/v1/status
*   Trying 10.20.30.5...
* Connected to rb-poc.internal.redwood (10.20.30.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=corp-proxy.local
* SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'rb-poc.internal.redwood'
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'rb-poc.internal.redwood'
```

Openssl:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.5:443 -servername rb-poc.internal.redwood
CONNECTED
depth=0 CN = corp-proxy.local
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=corp-proxy.local
issuer=/CN=corp-proxy-ca
---
SSL handshake has read 3872 bytes and written 517 bytes
```
They also tried `curl --resolve rb-poc.internal.redwood:443:10.20.30.5` and still saw proxy cert.

Jamal (Eng): Classic TLS interception. Proxy terminates TLS and presents its cert (corp-proxy.local). Two issues: 1) SNI the proxy sends may differ or be missing, so our endpoint-router serves default cert; 2) source IPs collapse to proxy NAT which can trigger rate limits.

Katy (Security): From compliance: they should use CONNECT or add an allowlist for this POC domain. We can't accept customer private CA certs into our trust store.

Ravi (NetOps): Logs show calls mapped to NAT IP 10.99.8.7 and we hit per-IP limits causing intermittent 429s. That matches their earlier reports.

Anya (Sales): They can't disable interception globally. They can add a proxy exception for a narrow set of domains. Is that sufficient?

Jamal (Eng): Yes. Short-term fixes: 
- Add a proxy exception so the client uses CONNECT/passthrough for rb-poc.internal.redwood (no MITM). That preserves SNI and the real cert.
- If CONNECT impossible, add our endpoint to a proxy skip-list and ensure the appliance forwards SNI and Host unchanged.

Ravi (NetOps): Also need them to whitelist our ENI IPs and health-probe CIDR in their egress firewall. And if SNAT collapses many users into one IP, either increase SNAT pool or we can open a temporary rate-limit exception.

infra-bot: support:temporary-rate-limit-exemption ticket 1802002610 created for project:retailbank-poc

Anya (Sales): They opened a change with the proxy team; ETA 8h for rule deployment.

(8 hours later) Anya (Sales): Proxy exception applied, retested: correct cert now presented, 502s gone. They saw one 429 from shared SNAT; infra-bot ticket created.

Ravi (NetOps): Confirmed: requests now show proper SNI and expected source IP ranges. We applied a temporary rate-limit exemption while they expand SNAT.

Katy (Security): Verified no private CAs uploaded and proxy exception scoped narrowly. Good to close.

Anya (Sales): Closing thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
